newsitem.title: UK: Britain sees EU summit as unnecessary, harmless.
newsitem.headline: Britain sees EU summit as unnecessary, harmless.

text.p: Britain sees a summit meeting of European Union heads of government to be held on Saturday as unnecessary, but also unlikely to harm its interests, officials said on Wednesday.
"We regard it as not a necessary meeting, but we are not suspicious," one senior official said. "We are not expecting to be ambushed at the crossroads."

The special Dublin summit of the 15-nation bloc to discuss reform of the European Union will be held just three days before the opening of the annual conference of Britain's ruling Conservative Party.
Major, whose party trails the Labour opposition by more than 20 points in the polls, hopes for a conference display of unity ahead of an election he must call by next May.

But he knows the so-called "Eurosceptic" wing of the party would react furiously to any sign from the Dublin meeting that he might yield to EU pressure for increased powers being given to the Community at the expense of member state governments.

The meeting was demanded by France which said it would give new momentum to the inter-governmental conference (IGC) which is discussing such difficult issues as the possible abandonment of member state vetoes in taking key decisions on EU policy.
But the British officials said this did not mean that France would be pushing for decisions in particular areas before a further Dublin summit late this year.
"We have not got the sense that the French have a specific notion of precisely what they want to emerge (from Saturday's meeting)," one said.

French foreign minister Herve de Charette was meeting his German opposite number Klaus Kinkel in Paris on Wednesday. But the officials said they did not expect a French or Franco-German initiative at the summit.
British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind flies to Paris on Thursday for a pre-summit meeting with de Charette.
